title: Email: "400 cs NS 1000 mL Available Now, Ships Today"

fields.fromName: Brent Kessler | Heartland Critical Supply Partners
fields.subject: URGENT – 400 cs NS 1000 mL AVAILABLE NOW – ships today
fields.body:
Good morning, Purchasing Team,

We know the IV fluid situation is hitting Iowa hard today, so I'm reaching out to you first.

We have secured 400 cases of 0.9% Sodium Chloride 1000 mL (12/cs, 4,800 bags) from a hospital network overstock. Price is $78.00/bag. Payment by credit card or wire only. Once payment clears we can have the order in Fort Dodge by 18:00 today.

The lot list and pedigree will follow after payment. We are fully licensed (license copy available on request).

Please note: this offer goes to the next hospital at 11:00 CT. Volume this size will not last. Reply to this email or call my cell directly to lock it in. The card authorization form is attached for your convenience.

Thanks, and stay safe out there,

Brent
fields.signature:
Brent Kessler
Senior Account Executive, Acute Care
Heartland Critical Supply Partners
Cell: 800-555-0177
"Getting hospitals what they need, when they need it."

instructorNote: This is a red herring. The email gives no Iowa wholesale distributor license number, no DSCSA transaction information and no lot list, and the attachment is only a card authorization form. The Purchasing Manager and the Director of Pharmacy should check the seller's licensure and refuse the offer as gray market under Drug Shortage plan section 4. They should record the refusal and keep working on the manufacturer emergency allocation and loans from Webster Valley and North Iowa Memorial. Watch for anyone who lets the 11:00 deadline or the 4.9 days on hand push them toward paying.
